observations: body L1-L3: Ptolemy's distance of the Sun, 1210 radii, exceeds al-Battānī's greatest, 1146 (p. 257, L35), by 64, and 1210 : 64 = 18 29/32 (18,906), as printed. The parallax varies inversely as the distance, so the values of the Almagest are to be multiplied by 1210 : 1146, that is increased by 64/1146 = 1/17,9 of themselves: an eighteenth part, as concluded; 64/1210 = 1/18,9 is the increase as a part of the increased parallax. «al–Battānī» (L2) has a long dash (5.3 pt); the t of «Almagesto» prints only in its upper part.
body L4-L6: 206 265″ : 23430 = 8″,803; the parallax 8″,80, adopted at the Paris conference of 1896, belongs to 23 440 radii, so «circiter».
body L7: 2′ 51″ answers to the distance of 1210 radii: arcsin (1 : 1210) = 2′ 50″,5. «al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L8-L9: 60ᵖ : 1146 = 0ᵖ 3′ 8″ 29‴ (3′ 8″,48) and 60ᵖ : 1070 = 0ᵖ 3′ 21″ 52‴ (3′ 21″,87); the arcs of which these are the sines measure 3′ 0″,0 and 3′ 12″,8: as printed. The formulas stand where they are printed, the 0″ of L8 over the 13″ of L9.

body L10: «p. 80.» has a full stop where the other references have a comma; the thirteen seconds are on the last line of p. 80 («e 13 secundis quibus parallaxis Solis ab apogeo ad perigeum differt»), 3′ 13″ − 3′ 0″. A short stroke prints below the a and the t of «memoratur».

body L11-L12: the dash after «n)» measures 10.2 pt, the hyphen of «4-6» 3.2 pt. The rules of p. 81, L4-L6 (the parallax in altitude times the sine of the angle of longitude, or of latitude, divided by 60ᵖ) are the formulas of note a), p. 251.
body L13: the dash after «o)» measures 10.0 pt, the hyphen of «23-34» 3.1 pt.

body L14-L20: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the meridian (radius 40.5 pt), the horizon from B, the vertical circle from the zenith to H and the ecliptic from G through H, as arcs of circles fitted to the print (radius 316.3, 80.1 and 152.5 pt), which meet in H within 0.04 pt; the words «Zenith», «horizon», «ecliptica» and «meridianus» and the letters G, B, H as printed, the last two words along their circles. The zenith, Z in L22, is marked only by the word.
body L18: «∓»: the northern declination of the culminating degree is subtracted from the latitude, the southern added (p. 81, L24-L25).

body L20-L29: (α) is the law of sines (p. 181, note 1) in the triangle GBH, right-angled at B, where the meridian meets the horizon: sin GHB = R sin GB : sin GH. GH is the distance of the Moon at the ascendant from the culminating degree, GB the meridian altitude of G, 90° − φ ± δ, whose sine is cos (φ ∓ δ); GHB, the angle of the ecliptic with the horizon, is the complement of ZHG, the vertical HZ being perpendicular to the horizon. It is al-Battānī's rule of p. 81, L23-L29. The label «(α)» stands at the left edge of the lines beside the figure and the formula where it is printed. In L27 the bar after «90°» (9.5 pt, as long as the signs of equality) is a minus sign, and the square brackets print taller than the parentheses.
body L29: «al-Battānī» has a hyphen (4.0 pt), shorter than the long dashes of L2 and L7 (5.3 pt).

body L30-L33: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition; «7–9» has a long dash (5.3 pt), the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 10.1 pt. The passage in italics is p. 81, L31-L33, for a latitude smaller than the northern declination of the culminating degree: sin ang. lat. = R sin (δ − φ) : sin dist. By (α), which holds in this case too, cos ang. lat. = R cos (δ − φ) : sin dist.; the two hold together only when the culminating degree is 90° from the ascendant, so the rule is false, as Schiaparelli says. The error of p. 80, L7-L9 is note l), p. 257.
body L34: the dash after «p)» measures 10.2 pt, that of «38—pag.» 10.0 pt; the stop after «pag» prints small and low.

body L35-L37: on the meridian the vertical circle through the Moon is the meridian itself, and the angle of latitude is the angle η of the ecliptic with the meridian. In the right spherical triangle of the ecliptic, the equator and the meridian, with the hypotenuse λ, the distance from Aries or Libra, and the side δ, the declination, cos η = tan δ : tan λ = sin δ cos λ : (cos δ sin λ), which is (α). It is al-Battānī's rule of p. 81, L40 - p. 82, L3. The label «(α)» stands at the margin and the formula where it is printed.
